title: Prompt Lattice Experimentarium
content:
Topline: a living scratchbook for trying combinatorial prompt variants (the "lattice") across task families where brittleness shows up: instruction ambiguity, few-shot ordering, and prefix leakage.

Goal: carve a small, reusable set of pattern primitives (literals, scaffolds, constraints) that we can mix-and-match and quickly A/B with the hosted API. Capture failure modes and small-heal heuristics.

Hypotheses:
- H1: separating role/context blocks from example blocks reduces prefix-leakage for completions when sequence length > 600 tokens.
- H2: explicit label markers (<<OUTPUT>>) reduce hallucinated field names in structured JSON output.
- H3: 3-shot semantically diverse exemplars outperform 5-shot similar exemplars on robustness to paraphrase prompts.

Quick checklist for running a variant:
- [ ] Pick lattice nodes: {system, persona, instructions, examples, output-marker, constraints}
- [ ] Choose temperature / top_p sweep (0.0, 0.2, 0.7)
- [ ] Run on canonical eval set (n=40) and random paraphrase set (n=80)
- [ ] Record: pass_rate, token_cost, top-1 semantic match, common hallucinations

Lattice primitives (working names):
- S: System + global context (single-line) e.g. "You are a terse assistant specialized in summarization."
- P: Persona tag e.g. "Assistant persona: product-owner-friendly, no code unless asked."
- I: Instruction block (task definition)
- E: Example block (few-shot exemplar(s)) with input/output markers
- M: Output marker (explicit token like "<<RESPONSE>>")
- C: Constraint block (format, tokens, disallowed phrases)

Experiment matrix samples (recorded runs):
1) Variant: S + I + E(3 diverse) + M + C
   - prompt: [system] You are a concise summarizer. [instruction] Summarize the article into 3 bullets. [examples] 3 diverse article->3 bullets examples. [<<RESPONSE>>]
   - notes: produced reasonable bullets; model sometimes invented one extra item when articles contained lists.
   - failure-mode: list inflation (model makes up count)
   - small heuristic: add constraint "Do not add items not present in source" (improves precision but cuts recall)

2) Variant: S + P + I + E(5 similar) + M
   - notes: repetition observed across examples (verbatim mimicry), output length drifted upward.
   - failure-mode: overfitting to example phrasing (template bleed)
   - mitigation: shuffle exemplar order, introduce negative exemplar showing "bad answer" style

FEW-SHOT SET A (for structured extraction):
- EX1 IN: "Article: 
Title: Tiny company achieves big things
Body: ..."
  OUT: {"title":"Tiny company achieves big things", "summary":"X"}
- EX2 IN: "Article: 
Title: New GPU runtime released
Body: ..."
  OUT: {"title":"New GPU runtime released", "summary":"Y"}
- EX3 IN: "Article: 
Title: Feature flags for autoscaling
Body: ..."
  OUT: {"title":"Feature flags for autoscaling", "summary":"Z"}

Notes on FEW-SHOT SET A: make sure examples include braces and double quotes exactly; model sometimes outputs single-quoted dicts. Add constraint: "Output must be valid JSON using double quotes". Also try explicit "return only JSON" marker.

Observed failure case: when the body contains parentheses or colon-heavy lines, the model nests arrays incorrectly ("summary" became array of tokens) — likely tokenization boundary causing truncation of exemplar mapping.

Micro-experiment: Prefix leakage test
- Setup: S contains 2-line system with long context (600+ tokens) + E(2) + I small.
- Result: completions reference earlier example ID strings present only in system context.
- Quick fix: move long context to "postamble" (append after M) and re-run — leakage drops but semantic relevance also drops. Trade-off noted.

Failure catalog (short):
- Hallucinated fields: model invents "author_affiliation" for some articles.
- Count hallucination: outputs 4 bullets when asked for 3.
- Type drift: asked for JSON, returns YAML-like block.
- Template bleed: reproduces exemplar wording exactly, even when source differs.

Heuristics that helped in runs: 
- Explicit output marker tokens (<<JSON>> / <<RESPONSE>>) provide small but consistent improvements for structured outputs.
- A negative exemplar (showing "incorrect" output) can teach the model what to avoid.
- For long contexts, prefer KV-cache-friendly segmentation: push non-essential context to an STERN_SHORT summary first and full text as an "attachment" in postamble.

Open questions / TODOs:
- [ ] Formalize a lightweight metric for "template-bleed": percentage of output n-grams identical to exemplars.
- [ ] Automate exemplar shuffling + re-weighting sweep; integrate with Redwood Optimize suggestions API.
- [ ] Try "label sandwich" pattern: label-examples-label (I think reduces count-hallucination).
- [ ] Evaluate effect of output-marker tokens across quantized models (4-bit) vs full precision.

Quick paste: sample prompt (copyable)

--PROMPT START--
You are a succinct assistant that returns only valid JSON.
Instruction: extract title and a 2-line summary.
Example 1:
Input: "Title: Tiny company achieves big things
Body: Startup scaled from 2 to 50 in 18 months..."
Output: {"title":"Tiny company achieves big things", "summary":"Scaled from 2 to 50 in 18 months"}
<<JSON>>
--PROMPT END--

Quick results snippet (n=40 canonical test):
- pass_rate (exact JSON match): 0.62
- pass_rate (semantic match): 0.82
- median tokens: 48
- common error: extra field "author_affiliation" in 8/40

Notes-to-self: when saving final lattice configs, include a short label that encodes nodes used (e.g. S_P_I_E3_M_C). Use that as experiment id.

Scratch ideas to try:
- Try "zero-shot with schema only" vs "1 shot with schema" to measure schema induction costs.
- Use a micro-LLM comparator (open-llm small) to filter hallucinated candidate fields before returning to user.

Related references: see linked PR for the run harness and PE-321 for ticket about schema markers.

End of scratchpad.
